events.body:
## Summary
`publishRepositoryToCatalog` (MainWindowRepos.cpp) is supposed to skip the network write when nothing a reader sees has changed: it hashes a `fingerprintSource` (with `updatedAt`, `lastSync`, `signature`, `catalogSig`, `stateSig`, `publishIntent` removed) and re-publishes an unchanged record only every `kCatalogPublishRefreshMs`, which is **6 hours**.

Observed instead: **311 POSTs in 194 minutes, one every 32 seconds**, metronomic, with an unchanging `stateHash`. So the fingerprint skip is not holding.

## Evidence
```
2026-08-03 14:55:29  Catalog: publishing forkmesh/forkmesh to .../api/repositories.
2026-08-03 14:56:01  Catalog: publishing forkmesh/forkmesh to .../api/repositories.
2026-08-03 14:56:33  Catalog: publishing forkmesh/forkmesh to .../api/repositories.
```
`Catalog publish request: jett forkmesh a8d6457b9e5d` -- same state hash across the whole window.

## Likely cause
Some field still inside `fingerprintSource` is volatile per attempt (a timestamp, a counter, a roster-derived value, or a size/artifact tally that jitters). The existing exclusion list covers only the six obviously per-attempt fields.

## Suggested direction
- Log the fingerprint delta once when a publish proceeds despite an apparently unchanged record, so the offending field names itself.
- Consider inverting the guard: hash an explicit allowlist of reader-visible fields rather than excluding known-volatile ones.

## Acceptance criteria
- An idle node with an unchanged repo publishes on the 6-hour refresh, not every 32s.
- A test asserts two consecutive publish attempts with identical reader-visible state produce one network write.

---
_Filed by Claude Code from the 2026-08-03 relay-quota investigation (node `jett`, 194-minute network_log window 11:42:43-14:57:00)._
events.title: Catalog record re-POSTs every 32s even though the unchanged-record guard is 6 hours
